detail: Dave asked "Can we swap out the mcp interface for a cli interface?" Assumption set for the assessment (unconfirmed by Dave): A1 the motivation is at least partly the Codex plugin's MCP path/cwd limitation documented today in docs/CODEX.md and docs/plans/2026-09-09-codex-plugin.md S1 (legacy Codex MCP does not expand plugin-root placeholders; portable MCP constrains cwd to plugin/data dirs, selecting the wrong store; automatic startup therefore uses npx). A2 "CLI interface" means the agent invokes a twining executable from its shell tool with subcommands mirroring the MCP tools and JSON output, not a human TUI. A3 "swap" is a hypothesis; adding a CLI beside MCP over a shared transport-agnostic command core is in scope as the alternative. A4 Gate-2 hook semantics (.last-record sentinel written by record/post/decide handlers, per-session activity marker) must be preserved by any new front-end. A5 the consumers whose constraints matter most are the field repo on Dave's other machine and the Codex port. Facts already established from Twining orientation: hooks are sentinel/marker based, not keyed on MCP tool names (decisions 01KQWCCVTV, 01KY3627YG); default surface is 5 core tools with 39 total registered under full_surface; the field's dominant outage class is the stdio server never starting (runner=none); a CLI subcommand dispatcher already exists (src/cli/dispatch.ts: migrate, validate-records). Investigation workflow wf_4271c5d9-7f0 launched with six readers plus one worktree-isolated measurement agent.
summary: CLI-vs-MCP assessment started 2026-09-09; the in-flight Codex plugin documents that Codex MCP configs cannot bind the bundled server to the project cwd — the concrete pain a CLI could avoid
